claims.text: Detection as direct set prediction: bipartite Hungarian matching loss (class NLL + L1 + scale-invariant GIoU box loss) plus Transformer encoder-decoder with learned object queries and parallel decoding; no anchors, no NMS, no specialized libraries.
claims.context: Full-paper sections 1/3.1/3.2 including loss equations and FFN/auxiliary-loss design.

claims.text: Results: COCO-val parity with heavily-tuned Faster R-CNN at equal parameters (42 AP R50, 44.9 DC5-R101); large-object dominance APL +7.8 attributed to global self-attention; small-object deficit APS -5.5; panoptic extension competitive (46 PQ test) especially on stuff classes.
claims.context: Full-paper sections 4.1/4.4 Tables 1/5; strengths and deficits both paper-stated.

claims.text: Costs stated by the paper: 300-500-epoch AdamW schedules (3 days on 16 V100), auxiliary decoding losses required, object-query slot specialization, NMS provably unnecessary only from later decoder layers (self-attention duplicate inhibition).
claims.context: Sections 4.1/4.2 ablations (encoder layers, decoder layers, FFN, positional encodings, NMS study) + conclusion challenges paragraph.

limitations: Small-object deficit and training cost are paper-stated open challenges; FPN-style successors address them outside this source.

verification.finding: Full body consumed: loss formulation, architecture, COCO tables, ablations, panoptic extension, and stated challenges verified.
